one_liner: Research OmpSs/OpenMP-task parallelization of CHOLMOD's supernodal Cholesky with selective nesting; 1.95x over multi-threaded-BLAS CHOLMOD on A64FX.
what_it_does: A research re-parallelization of the numerical factorization phase of CHOLMOD's supernodal sparse Cholesky, using one outer task per supernode and optional nested inner tasks for the SYRK/GEMM updates from predecessor supernodes. It is not a library with a stable API: it ships as a Zenodo archive (selective-nesting-main.zip) with source, raw data and plotting scripts for the paper's experiments. Analysis (ordering, elimination tree, amalgamation) and solve phases are CHOLMOD's.
how_it_is_fast: Stock CHOLMOD walks supernodes in order and gets parallelism only from multi-threaded BLAS inside each supernode, which starves on small or very sparse fronts. This work exposes elimination-tree parallelism as tasks and uses 'selective nesting': an outer task is split into inner update tasks only if it has at least D updates (D picked per matrix by the OPT-D heuristic targeting max(1.1*n_super, n/14) tasks), and OPT-D-COST additionally suppresses inner tasks under about 50,000 flops to cut runtime overhead. Nesting is toggled with the OpenMP 'final' clause.
when_to_use: You run CHOLMOD-style supernodal Cholesky on many-core Arm A64FX (Fugaku/FX1000/FX700) and multi-threaded BLAS leaves cores idle.
Large SPD matrices (millions of nonzeros) where the paper reports 1.67-1.83x over its non-nested task baseline.
Matrices with wide, shallow elimination trees where mt-BLAS CHOLMOD collapses (e.g. af_shell3: mt-BLAS 0.19x vs OPT-D-COST 1.31x relative to non-nested).
As a reference design for adding task-granularity control to your own supernodal or multifrontal factorization.
when_not_to_use: Production code: it is a paper artifact under CC-BY-4.0 (not an OSI software license), with no releases, tests or maintenance.
x86 or GPU machines: only A64FX was evaluated; the authors say thresholds (n/14 goal, 50,000-flop cutoff, D <= 30% of max children) were tuned there and would need re-tuning for x86.
Small matrices (10k-200k nonzeros): gain over the non-nested task version is only about 1.07x.
Toolchains without OmpSs-1 (nanos++/mercurium) unless you port the pragmas to plain OpenMP tasks yourself.
If you need a maintained faster Cholesky, BaSpaCho or Sympiler are catalogued with real repositories.

integration.dependencies: CHOLMOD (SuiteSparse, version not stated), OmpSs-1 19.06 (nanos++ runtime, mercurium compiler), vendor BLAS/LAPACK (Fujitsu BLAS in the paper)
integration.platforms: evaluated only on aarch64 A64FX (48 cores, HBM2)
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — replaces CHOLMOD's numerical factorization internals, but it is not packaged as a patch or library; integration method is not documented

gotchas: The 1.46x headline is against the authors' own non-nested task version (equivalent to PaStiX-style 1D task decomposition), not against an external library; 1.95x vs mt-BLAS CHOLMOD is the same data (mt-BLAS averages 0.75x of non-nested).
Always-nested tasks run out of memory on 7 large matrices; selective nesting avoids that, so the D threshold also matters for memory.
Heuristic constants are empirical and hard-coded; the paper adds further hand-written hybrid conditions (average supernode size > 50, density < 1e-4).
CHOLMOD version and compiler flags are not stated, so reproducing the numbers needs the archive's scripts.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over BaSpaCho or Sympiler only if you are staying inside CHOLMOD on A64FX and want its task-granularity heuristics; otherwise those siblings are maintained libraries with code you can actually depend on.
verified_claims_summary: On a 48-core 4-socket A64FX (2.2 GHz, 32 GB HBM2) with fcc 4.2.0b, OmpSs-1 19.06 and Fujitsu BLAS, OPT-D-COST averaged 1.46x over a non-nested task-parallel CHOLMOD and 1.95x over stock CHOLMOD with multi-threaded BLAS across 60 SuiteSparse SPD matrices (about 1.07x on small, up to 1.83x on large groups).
status_note: One-off research artifact (Zenodo v3, Oct 2021; paper arXiv 2202.09288, also presented at ESPM2'22) with no ongoing maintenance; reference-only because the artifact is CC-BY-4.0 rather than a software license.
